slides.headline: He noticed why the sea looks blue - and became the first Asian ever to win a Nobel Prize in science.
Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman was born November 7, 1888, in Tiruchirappalli, Madras Presidency.
slides.body: In 1930, he won the Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering what's now called the Raman Effect - how light scatters when it passes through a transparent material, revealing that material's molecular structure.

slides.headline: He was the first Asian, and the first non-white person, to win a Nobel Prize in any science.
slides.body: The discovery came from pure curiosity about something as ordinary as the color of the sea - and it's still used today in chemistry, materials science, and medical diagnostics through Raman spectroscopy.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat still runs on the same curiosity Raman brought to an ordinary question nearly a century ago.
slides.body: His Nobel wasn't the result of vast resources - it came from careful observation and a refusal to accept 'that's just how it is' as an answer.
